main_text.p: Si luteum Procne sub trabe figat opus. Si trabibus laxam suspendit aranea casson, Esse putat nummis retia tensa suis. Si sol rimosas penetret, vel Luna fenestras, Fert tenuem fudit lux inopina diem: Oblinit extemplo rimas, ne scilicet auro Inficiat radios ille, vel illa suos. Nec minus obscuras formidat nocte tenebras, Et latebras promptas ad scelus omne ducès, Ipse suam veluti furem luctatur in umbram: Gypsatas metuunt credula corda manus. Huc labor, & miseri spectat vesania voti, Et trepidi semper corde micante metus. Post inopis curas, & inania tædia vita, Dives ut ad Stygias ibe feratur aquas. Atque opibus mortem seu placaturus anaram, Semper inops vivit, ne moriatur inops.
main_text.head: IOANNES STVRMIVS.
main_text.p: O Ra vides Sturmi, sed & hæc Germania sumit, Hæc pietas, Latio cum lubet ore loqui. Hæc Hermes: also citius nec se putat ore Flectere posse homines, flectere posse deos.
main_text.head: IDEM.
main_text.p: O Ra hæc sunt Sturmi pictura verba darentur Si sua, de Phæbi pectore missa putes. Nec falso expulsus iamdudum Phocidos antro In Sturmi sedem pectore Phœbus habet.
main_text.head: IDEM.
main_text.p: N Il refert, Sturmi hæc, an Phæbi dixeris ora: Hoc Phœbus solet, hoc Sturmus ore loqui.

page.notes: The first word of each verse-paragraph is a large woodcut initial (O, O, N) and is transcribed as the letter with the word; the first line of the page is partly printed in italic and the initial letters of the first two lines are uncertain. Right margin shows show-through and edge marks, not transcribed. Some letters such as "s" long s are normalised to s; "si" in "si luteum" read as "Si".
